export async function getCommentThreads(
  pg: SupabaseDirectClient,
  filters: {
    contractId: string
    limit: number
    page: number
  }
) {
  const { contractId, limit, page } = filters

  const allComments = await pg.map(
    `
    with parent_comments as (
      select cc.data, cc.likes, cc.comment_id from contract_comments cc
      where cc.contract_id = $1
      and (cc.data->>'replyToCommentId' is null)
      and (cc.data->>'deleted' is null or cc.data->>'deleted' = 'false')
      order by cc.created_time desc
      limit $2
      offset $3
    )
    select * from parent_comments
    union all
    select cc.data, cc.likes, cc.comment_id from contract_comments cc
    where cc.contract_id = $1
    and (cc.data->>'replyToCommentId' in (select comment_id from parent_comments))
    and (cc.data->>'deleted' is null or cc.data->>'deleted' = 'false')
    `,
    [contractId, limit, page * limit],
    convertContractComment
  )

  const parentComments = allComments.filter((c) => !c.replyToCommentId)
  const replyComments = allComments.filter((c) => c.replyToCommentId)
  console.log('parentComments', parentComments.length)
  console.log('replyComments', replyComments.length)

  return { parentComments, replyComments }
}

export async function getCommentThread(
  pg: SupabaseDirectClient,
  commentId: string,
  contractId: string
) {
  const comment = await pg.oneOrNone(
    `
      select cc.data, cc.likes from contract_comments cc
      where cc.comment_id = $1 and cc.contract_id = $2
    `,
    [commentId, contractId],
    convertContractComment
  )
  if (!comment) {
    return {
      parentComment: null,
      replyComments: [],
      parentComments: [],
      nextParentComments: [],
      nextReplyComments: [],
    }
  }

  const parentId = comment.replyToCommentId ?? comment.id
  const parentComment =
    comment.replyToCommentId && comment.replyToCommentId !== comment.id
      ? await pg.oneOrNone(
          `
      select cc.data, cc.likes from contract_comments cc
      where cc.comment_id = $1 and cc.contract_id = $2
    `,
          [parentId, contractId],
          convertContractComment
        )
      : comment

  if (!parentComment) {
    return {
      parentComment: null,
      replyComments: [],
      parentComments: [],
      nextParentComments: [],
      nextReplyComments: [],
    }
  }

  const results = await pg.multi(
    `
      select cc.data, cc.likes from contract_comments cc
      where cc.contract_id = $1
      and (cc.data->>'replyToCommentId' = $2)
      and (cc.data->>'deleted' is null or cc.data->>'deleted' = 'false')
      order by cc.created_time asc;
      select cc.data, cc.likes from contract_comments cc
      where cc.contract_id = $1
      and (cc.data->>'replyToCommentId' is null)
      and (cc.data->>'deleted' is null or cc.data->>'deleted' = 'false')
      and cc.created_time > $3
      order by cc.created_time desc;
      select cc.data, cc.likes from contract_comments cc
      where cc.contract_id = $1
      and (cc.data->>'replyToCommentId' is null)
      and (cc.data->>'deleted' is null or cc.data->>'deleted' = 'false')
      and cc.created_time < $3
      order by cc.created_time desc
      limit 3;
    `,
    [contractId, parentId, millisToTs(parentComment.createdTime)]
  )
  const replyComments = results[0].map(convertContractComment)
  const parentComments = results[1].map(convertContractComment)
  const nextParentComments = results[2].map(convertContractComment)

  const nextReplyComments =
    nextParentComments.length > 0
      ? await pg.map(
          `
      select cc.data, cc.likes from contract_comments cc
      where cc.contract_id = $1
      and (cc.data->>'replyToCommentId' in ($2:csv))
      and (cc.data->>'deleted' is null or cc.data->>'deleted' = 'false')
      order by cc.created_time asc
    `,
          [contractId, nextParentComments.map((c) => c.id)],
          convertContractComment
        )
      : []

  return {
    parentComment,
    replyComments,
    parentComments,
    nextParentComments,
    nextReplyComments,
  }
}

export async function getCommentsDirect(
  pg: SupabaseDirectClient,
  filters: {
    userId?: string
    contractId?: string
    limit?: number
    page?: number
    replyToCommentId?: string
    commentId?: string
    afterTime?: number
    order?: 'likes' | 'newest' | 'oldest'
  }
) {
  const {
    userId,
    contractId,
    limit = 5000,
    page = 0,
    replyToCommentId,
    commentId,
    afterTime,
    order = 'newest',
  } = filters

  const params: any[] = [
    limit,
    page * limit,
    contractId,
    userId,
    replyToCommentId,
    commentId,
    afterTime ? millisToTs(afterTime) : null,
  ]
  const orderBy =
    order === 'likes'
      ? 'cc.likes desc'
      : !order || order === 'newest'
      ? 'cc.created_time desc'
      : 'cc.created_time asc'

  return await pg.map(
    `
        select cc.data, cc.likes from contract_comments cc
          join contracts c on cc.contract_id = c.id
        where c.visibility = 'public'
          and ($3 is null or contract_id = $3)
          and ($4 is null or user_id = $4)
          and ($5 is null or cc.data->>'replyToCommentId' = $5) 
          and ($6 is null or cc.comment_id = $6)          
          and ($7 is null or cc.created_time > $7)
          and (cc.data->>'deleted' is null or cc.data->>'deleted' = 'false')        
        order by ${orderBy}
        limit $1
        offset $2
    `,
    params,
    convertContractComment
  )
}

export async function getPostAndContractComments(
  pg: SupabaseDirectClient,
  filters: {
    userId: string
    limit?: number
    page?: number
    afterTime?: number
  }
): Promise<(ContractComment | PostComment)[]> {
  const { userId, limit = 5000, page = 0, afterTime } = filters

  const params: any[] = [
    limit,
    page * limit,
    userId,
    afterTime ? millisToTs(afterTime) : null,
  ]

  const query = `
      SELECT * FROM (
        -- Contract Comments
        SELECT
            cc.data,
            cc.created_time,
            cc.comment_id,
            c.slug,
            c.question as title
        FROM contract_comments cc
        JOIN contracts c ON cc.contract_id = c.id
        WHERE
            c.visibility = 'public'
            AND cc.user_id = $3                   -- userId (must be present here)
            AND ($4 IS NULL OR cc.created_time > $4) -- afterTime
            AND (cc.data->>'deleted' IS NULL OR cc.data->>'deleted' = 'false')
            
        UNION ALL

        -- Old Post Comments
        SELECT
            opc.data,
            opc.created_time,
            opc.comment_id,
            op.data->>'slug' as slug,
            op.data->>'title' as title
        FROM old_post_comments opc
        join old_posts op on opc.post_id = op.id
        WHERE
            opc.user_id = $3
            AND ($4 IS NULL OR opc.created_time > $4)
            and op.visibility = 'public'
      ) AS combined_comments
      ORDER BY created_time DESC
      LIMIT $1 -- limit
      OFFSET $2 -- offset
    `

  return await pg.map(query, params, (r) => {
    const comment = r.data as ContractComment | PostComment
    if (comment.commentType === 'post') {
      comment.postSlug = r.slug
      comment.postTitle = r.title
    }
    return comment
  })
}

export type ValidatedAPIParams<N extends APIPath> = z.output<
  APISchema<N>['props']
>

export type APIResponse<N extends APIPath> = APISchema<N> extends {
  returns: Record<string, any>
}
  ? APISchema<N>['returns']
  : void

export type APIResponseOptionalContinue<N extends APIPath> =
  | { continue: () => Promise<void>; result: APIResponse<N> }
  | APIResponse<N>

  | APIResponse<N>

evalCommits.spec:
Implement a portfolio history downsampling system with the following components:

## Database Schema Changes
1. Create a `portfolios_processed` table with columns:
   - `user_id` (text, primary key)
   - `last_processed` (timestamp with time zone, defaults to now())
   - Enable row level security

2. Create a `user_portfolio_history_archive` table with the same structure as the existing `user_portfolio_history` table:
   - All the same columns (balance, cash_balance, investment_value, etc.)
   - `id` as auto-incrementing primary key
   - `user_id` and `ts` fields
   - Enable row level security with public read policy

## Portfolio History Downsampling Function
Create a `downsamplePortfolioHistory` function that:
1. Identifies users who need processing by finding users who:
   - Have betting activity (lastBetTime exists)
   - Were created more than 1 month ago
   - Haven't been processed recently (either never processed or last processed more than 1 week ago)

2. For each user, find days with more than 4 portfolio history entries that are older than 1 month

3. For each user-day combination needing processing:
   - Delete the detailed portfolio history records from the main table
   - Insert those deleted records into the archive table
   - Create new downsampled records by grouping the deleted data into 6-hour intervals (0-6h, 6-12h, 12-18h, 18-24h) and averaging the values
   - Insert the downsampled records back into the main portfolio history table

4. Track processing completion in the `portfolios_processed` table

5. Include appropriate logging and use database transactions for data integrity

## Job Scheduler Updates
1. Add a new scheduled job called 'downsample-portfolio-history' that runs daily at 4:50am
2. Remove the 'update-cash-stats' job from the scheduler
3. Reorganize imports in alphabetical order

## API Endpoint Updates
Modify the `getUserPortfolioHistory` API endpoint to handle the 'allTime' period by:
1. Running two separate database queries when period is 'allTime':
   - One query for recent data (last month using monthly cutoff)
   - One query for older historical data
2. Use `pg.multi()` instead of `pg.map()` to execute multiple queries
3. Combine results from both queries before sorting and returning
4. For non-allTime periods, maintain existing behavior but use the updated query structure

The system should preserve data integrity while reducing storage requirements for old portfolio history data, and ensure the API continues to provide comprehensive historical data when requested.

import { sortBy } from 'lodash'

import { type APIHandler } from './helpers/endpoint'
import { createSupabaseDirectClient } from 'shared/supabase/init'
import { getCutoff } from 'common/period'
import { convertPortfolioHistory } from 'common/supabase/portfolio-metrics'

export const getUserPortfolioHistory: APIHandler<
  'get-user-portfolio-history'
> = async (props) => {
  const pg = createSupabaseDirectClient()
  const { userId, period } = props

  const startDate = new Date(getCutoff(period)).toISOString()

  const data = await pg.map(
    `select *
    from user_portfolio_history
    where
      user_id = $1

import { sortBy } from 'lodash'

import { getCutoff } from 'common/period'
import { convertPortfolioHistory } from 'common/supabase/portfolio-metrics'
import { createSupabaseDirectClient } from 'shared/supabase/init'
import { type APIHandler } from './helpers/endpoint'

export const getUserPortfolioHistory: APIHandler<
  'get-user-portfolio-history'
> = async (props) => {
  const pg = createSupabaseDirectClient()
  const { userId, period } = props
  const isAllTime = period === 'allTime'
  const cutoff = isAllTime ? getCutoff('monthly') : getCutoff(period)

  const startDate = new Date(cutoff).toISOString()
  const allTimeQuery = isAllTime
    ? `select *
    from user_portfolio_history
    where
      user_id = $1
      and ts < now() - interval '1 month';`
    : ''
  const data = await pg.multi(
    `select *
    from user_portfolio_history
    where
      user_id = $1
      and ts > $2
    order by random()
    limit 1000;
    ${allTimeQuery}`,
    [userId, startDate]
  )
  const latestPoints = data[0].map(convertPortfolioHistory)
  const laterPoints = isAllTime ? data[1].map(convertPortfolioHistory) : []
  const allPoints = [...latestPoints, ...laterPoints]

  return sortBy(allPoints, 'timestamp')
}

import { createSupabaseDirectClient } from 'shared/supabase/init'
import { log } from 'shared/utils'

const TESTING = false
export async function downsamplePortfolioHistory() {
  const db = createSupabaseDirectClient()
  log('Starting portfolio history downsampling')
  const userIds = TESTING
    ? ['rZe5vReIBSYJpUymsFBWW1aUyp13']
    : await db.map(
        `select distinct id from users
            left join portfolios_processed p on p.user_id = users.id
            where data->>'lastBetTime' is not null
            and created_time < now() - interval '1 month'
            and (p.user_id is null or p.last_processed < now() - interval '1 week')`,
        [],
        (u) => u.id
      )
  log(`Downsampling portfolio history for ${userIds.length} users `)

  for (const userId of userIds) {
    await db.tx(async (tx) => {
      const daysToProcess = await tx.manyOrNone<{
        user_id: string
        day: string
      }>(
        `
        select p.user_id, p.day from (
          select
            user_id,
            date_trunc('day', ts) as day,
            count(*) as daily_count
          from user_portfolio_history
          where user_id = $1
          and ts < now() - interval '1 month'
          group by user_id, date_trunc('day', ts)
        ) as p
        where p.daily_count > 4
      `,
        [userId]
      )

      if (daysToProcess.length === 0) return

      log(`Found ${daysToProcess.length} user-days to process for ${userId}.`)

      const userIds = daysToProcess.map((d) => d.user_id)
      const days = daysToProcess.map((d) => d.day)

      await tx.none(
        `
      with
        days_to_process_unnested as (
          select *
          from unnest($1::text[], $2::timestamp[]) as t(user_id, day)
        ),
        points_to_process as (
          select p.id
          from user_portfolio_history p
            join days_to_process_unnested d
            on p.user_id = d.user_id
            and date_trunc('day', p.ts) = d.day
        ),
        deleted_points as (
          delete from user_portfolio_history
          where id in (select id from points_to_process)
          returning *
        ),
        archived_points as (
          insert into
            user_portfolio_history_archive (
              user_id,
              ts,
              balance,
              cash_balance,
              investment_value,
              total_deposits,
              loan_total,
              profit,
              cash_investment_value,
              total_cash_deposits,
              spice_balance
            )
          select
            user_id,
            ts,
            balance,
            cash_balance,
            investment_value,
            total_deposits,
            loan_total,
            profit,
            cash_investment_value,
            total_cash_deposits,
            spice_balance
          from deleted_points
        ),
        new_points as (
          select
            p.user_id,
            (
              date_trunc('day', p.ts) +
              (floor(extract(hour from p.ts) / 6) * interval '6 hours')
            ) as ts,
            avg(p.balance) as balance,
            avg(p.cash_balance) as cash_balance,
            avg(p.cash_investment_value) as cash_investment_value,
            avg(p.investment_value) as investment_value,
            avg(p.loan_total) as loan_total,
            avg(p.profit) as profit,
            avg(p.spice_balance) as spice_balance,
            avg(p.total_cash_deposits) as total_cash_deposits,
            avg(p.total_deposits) as total_deposits
          from deleted_points p
          group by
            p.user_id,
            date_trunc('day', p.ts),
            floor(extract(hour from p.ts) / 6)
        )
      insert into
        user_portfolio_history (
          user_id,
          ts,
          balance,
          cash_balance,
          cash_investment_value,
          investment_value,
          loan_total,
          profit,
          spice_balance,
          total_cash_deposits,
          total_deposits
        )
      select
        user_id,
        ts,
        balance,
        cash_balance,
        cash_investment_value,
        investment_value,
        loan_total,
        profit,
        spice_balance,
        total_cash_deposits,
        total_deposits
      from new_points
      `,
        [userIds, days]
      )
      await tx.none(
        `
        insert into portfolios_processed (user_id)
        values ($1) on conflict (user_id) do update set last_processed = now()
        `,
        [userId]
      )
    })
  }
  log('Finished portfolio history downsampling')
}

Implement solid icon variants for active navigation states in the bottom navigation bar and related components:

1. **Navigation Item Type Enhancement**:
   - Add a `solidIcon` property to the NavItem type definition that accepts the same type as the existing `icon` property

2. **Bottom Navigation Bar Icon System**:
   - Import solid versions of navigation icons from heroicons/solid and react-icons libraries
   - Add solid icon variants to all navigation items in both signed-in and signed-out navigation configurations
   - Implement logic to display the solid icon variant when a navigation item represents the current active page, falling back to the outline icon when inactive or when no solid variant is available

3. **NotificationsIcon Component Updates**:
   - Replace the existing heroicons BellIcon with react-icons IoNotifications variants (IoNotificationsOutline and IoNotifications)
   - Add a `solid` boolean prop that switches between outline and solid notification icon variants
   - Create wrapper components that pass the appropriate solid/outline state to work with the navigation system

4. **Visual Style Updates**:
   - Update the default icon sizing in navigation from `h-7 w-7` to `h-[1.6rem] w-[1.6rem]`
   - Remove the background color (`bg-ink-100`) from the selected item styling, keeping only the text color change
   - Change the touch feedback class name from a descriptive class to `touch-press-effect`

5. **Profile Navigation Enhancements**:
   - Add a violet ring border around the user avatar when the user is currently on their own profile page
   - Remove the cash balance (sweepies) display from the profile navigation item, keeping only the main balance
   - Adjust the positioning and styling of the remaining token display

6. **Touch Animation CSS**:
   - Add CSS keyframe animations for touch feedback including `bounce-press`, `touch-press-bounce` 
   - Implement corresponding CSS classes: `touch-bounce`, `touch-scale-down`, `touch-press-effect`, and `touch-release`
   - Design the animations to provide visual feedback when users interact with touch-enabled navigation elements

The implementation should maintain backward compatibility while enhancing the visual feedback for active navigation states and touch interactions.

The system needs to implement a "New Comments" sorting option for posts that allows users to view posts ordered by their most recent comment activity.

## Backend API Changes

The `get-posts` API endpoint needs to support a new sorting option:
- Add 'new-comments' as a valid value for the `sortBy` parameter (in addition to existing 'created_time' and 'importance_score' options)
- When `sortBy` is set to 'new-comments', posts should be ordered by their last comment time in descending order, with posts that have no comments appearing last (NULLS LAST behavior)
- The existing ordering logic should remain unchanged for other sortBy values

## Frontend UI Changes

The posts page needs to include a new sorting tab:
- Add a "New Comments" button/tab alongside the existing "Best", "New", and "Changelog" options
- When selected, this should fetch posts using the 'new-comments' sortBy parameter
- The button should follow the same styling and behavior patterns as existing sort buttons (highlighted when active)

## Post Card Display Changes

Post cards need to always show activity time:
- The "Active" timestamp should display the last comment time when available
- When no comments exist on a post, it should fall back to showing the post creation time
- Remove any conditional rendering that hides the "Active" timestamp when there are no comments

## Data Flow

- The posts page should detect when a different sort option is selected and fetch new data accordingly
- The 'best' posts can continue to use cached/static data
- All other sort options (including the new 'new-comments') should trigger fresh API calls
- The sorting parameter should be properly mapped based on the selected view type

The implementation should maintain consistency with existing patterns for API parameters, UI styling, and data fetching behavior.

import { APIHandler } from 'api/helpers/endpoint'
import { convertPost, TopLevelPost } from 'common/top-level-post'
import { buildArray } from 'common/util/array'
import { createSupabaseDirectClient } from 'shared/supabase/init'
import {
  from,
  groupBy,
  leftJoin,
  limit as limitSql,
  orderBy,
  renderSql,
  select,
  where,
} from 'shared/supabase/sql-builder'
export const getPosts: APIHandler<'get-posts'> = async (props, auth) => {
  const {
    sortBy = 'created_time',
    term,
    limit,
    userId,
    offset,
    isChangeLog,
  } = props
  const requester = auth?.uid
  const pg = createSupabaseDirectClient()

  const sqlParts = buildArray(
    select(
      'op.*, count(distinct opc.user_id) as comment_count, count(distinct r.user_id) as reaction_count, max(opc.created_time) as last_comment_time'
    ),
    from('old_posts op'),
    leftJoin('old_post_comments opc on op.id = opc.post_id'),
    leftJoin('user_reactions r on op.id = r.content_id'),
    (userId !== requester || !requester) && where(`op.visibility = 'public'`),
    where(`op.group_id is null`),
    isChangeLog && where(`(op.data->>'isChangeLog')::boolean = true`),
    userId && where(`op.creator_id = $1`),
    term &&
      term.trim().length > 0 &&
      where(
        `to_tsvector('english', op.data->>'title') @@ websearch_to_tsquery('english', $2)`
      ),
    groupBy('op.id'),
    orderBy(`op.${sortBy} DESC`),
    limitSql(limit, offset)
  )

  const query = renderSql(...sqlParts)
  const data = await pg.manyOrNone(query, [userId, term])
  return data.map((d) => ({
    ...convertPost(d),
    reactionCount: d.reaction_count,
    commentCount: d.comment_count,
    lastCommentTime: d.last_comment_time
      ? Date.parse(d.last_comment_time)
      : null,
    uniqueUsers: d.reaction_count + d.comment_count,
  })) as TopLevelPost[]
}

  const requester = auth?.uid
  const pg = createSupabaseDirectClient()

  const sqlParts = buildArray(
    select(
      'op.*, count(distinct opc.user_id) as comment_count, count(distinct r.user_id) as reaction_count, max(opc.created_time) as last_comment_time'

  // GET is for retrieval, POST is to mutate something, PUT is idempotent mutation (can be repeated safely)
  method: 'GET' | 'POST' | 'PUT'
  //private APIs can only be called from manifold. undocumented endpoints can change or be deleted at any time!
  visibility: 'public' | 'undocumented' | 'private'
  // whether the endpoint requires authentication
  authed: boolean
  // zod schema for the request body (or for params for GET requests)
  props: z.ZodType
  // note this has to be JSON serializable
  returns?: Record<string, any>
  // Cache-Control header. like, 'max-age=60'
  cache?: string

  preferAuth?: boolean

export type APIPath = keyof typeof API
export type APISchema<N extends APIPath> = (typeof API)[N]

export type APIParams<N extends APIPath> = z.input<APISchema<N>['props']>
export type ValidatedAPIParams<N extends APIPath> = z.output<
  APISchema<N>['props']
>

export type APIResponse<N extends APIPath> = APISchema<N> extends {
  returns: Record<string, any>
}
  ? APISchema<N>['returns']
  : void

export type APIResponseOptionalContinue<N extends APIPath> =
  | { continue: () => Promise<void>; result: APIResponse<N> }
  | APIResponse<N>

The system needs to implement the following changes to support displaying last comment activity time for posts and improve the post card UI:

## Backend API Changes

### Update get-posts endpoint
- Modify the SQL query in the get-posts endpoint to include the maximum comment creation time
- Add `max(opc.created_time) as last_comment_time` to the SELECT clause
- In the response mapping, add a `lastCommentTime` field that converts the SQL timestamp to a JavaScript timestamp (using `Date.parse()`) or null if no comments exist

## Type Definition Updates

### Update TopLevelPost type
- Add an optional `lastCommentTime` field of type `number | null` to the TopLevelPost interface
- Mark this field as deprecated with comment indicating it's only available via the get-posts endpoint

## Frontend Component Changes

### Simplify PostCard component interface
- Remove the `onPostClick` callback parameter from the PostCard component
- Remove conditional click handling logic - always use Next.js Link for navigation
- Remove the `onPostClick` parameter from PostCardList component as well

### Add last activity display
- When `lastCommentTime` is available on a post, display "Active {time ago}" text in the post card header area
- Use the existing `fromNow` utility function to format the relative time

### Replace admin button with dropdown menu
- Replace the standalone "Make Unlisted" button for admin/mod users with a dropdown menu
- Use the existing DropdownMenu component with a DotsHorizontalIcon trigger
- Include the unlist/list action as a menu item with an EyeOffIcon
- Use the `buildArray` utility to conditionally include menu items based on user permissions
- Position the dropdown in the top-right area of the post card header

### Code organization improvements
- Reorganize imports to follow the established pattern: external library imports first, followed by a blank line, then internal imports sorted alphabetically
- Remove unused props and state (like loading states that are now handled by the dropdown)

The changes should maintain all existing functionality while adding the new last activity display and improving the admin interface through the dropdown menu.

import { APIHandler } from 'api/helpers/endpoint'
import { convertPost, TopLevelPost } from 'common/top-level-post'
import { buildArray } from 'common/util/array'
import { createSupabaseDirectClient } from 'shared/supabase/init'
import {
  from,
  groupBy,
  leftJoin,
  limit as limitSql,
  orderBy,
  renderSql,
  select,
  where,
} from 'shared/supabase/sql-builder'
export const getPosts: APIHandler<'get-posts'> = async (props, auth) => {
  const {
    sortBy = 'created_time',
    term,
    limit,
    userId,
    offset,
    isChangeLog,
  } = props
  const requester = auth?.uid
  const pg = createSupabaseDirectClient()

  const sqlParts = buildArray(
    select(
      'op.*, count(distinct opc.user_id) as comment_count, count(distinct r.user_id) as reaction_count, max(opc.created_time) as last_comment_time'
    ),
    from('old_posts op'),
    leftJoin('old_post_comments opc on op.id = opc.post_id'),
    leftJoin('user_reactions r on op.id = r.content_id'),
    (userId !== requester || !requester) && where(`op.visibility = 'public'`),
    where(`op.group_id is null`),
    isChangeLog && where(`(op.data->>'isChangeLog')::boolean = true`),
    userId && where(`op.creator_id = $1`),
    term &&
      term.trim().length > 0 &&
      where(
        `to_tsvector('english', op.data->>'title') @@ websearch_to_tsquery('english', $2)`
      ),
    groupBy('op.id'),
    orderBy(`op.${sortBy} DESC`),
    limitSql(limit, offset)
  )

  const query = renderSql(...sqlParts)
  const data = await pg.manyOrNone(query, [userId, term])
  return data.map((d) => ({
    ...convertPost(d),
    reactionCount: d.reaction_count,
    commentCount: d.comment_count,
    lastCommentTime: d.last_comment_time
      ? Date.parse(d.last_comment_time)
      : null,
    uniqueUsers: d.reaction_count + d.comment_count,
  })) as TopLevelPost[]
}

The DailyLoan and DailyProfit components need to be refactored to remove unnecessary wrapper elements and flatten their component structure.

**DailyLoan Component Changes:**
When `showChest` is true, the component currently renders a `Col` wrapper element that contains a `Tooltip` with a `button` inside. This needs to be restructured so that:
- The `Col` wrapper element is removed entirely
- The `Tooltip` becomes the direct child of a React Fragment
- The `button` element inside the Tooltip receives all the className properties that were previously applied to the `Col` wrapper
- The overall functionality and styling should remain identical, just with a flattened DOM structure

**DailyProfit Component Changes:**
The component currently renders a `div` wrapper with `dailyStatsClass` that contains a `Row` with gap-2, which in turn contains a `button`. This needs to be restructured so that:
- The outer `div` wrapper is removed entirely  
- The `button` element becomes the top-level element and receives the `dailyStatsClass` that was previously on the div
- The `Row` element inside the button should no longer have the `gap-2` class
- The overall functionality and styling should remain identical, just with a flattened DOM structure

Both changes should maintain all existing functionality, event handlers, styling, and visual appearance while reducing DOM nesting depth.

The boost analytics system needs to be enhanced to display creator information for each boost period.

**Backend Changes:**
1. Modify the boost analytics API endpoint to join the `contract_boosts` table with the `users` table to retrieve creator information
2. Include the creator's name and username in the boost data returned by the API
3. Update the response structure so that each boost period includes `creatorName` and `creatorUsername` fields

**API Schema Changes:**
1. Update the return type specification for the `get-boost-analytics` endpoint in the API schema
2. Modify the `boostPeriods` array type to include `creatorName` and `creatorUsername` as string fields in addition to the existing `startTime` and `endTime` fields

**Frontend Changes:**
1. Update the TypeScript type definition for `BoostPeriod` to include optional `creatorName` and `creatorUsername` properties
2. Modify the boost period display logic to show creator information when available
3. Display the creator's name as a clickable link that navigates to their profile page
4. Format the boost period display to show: "[start date] - [end date] by [creator name]" where the creator name links to `/{creatorUsername}`
5. Handle cases where creator information might not be available (make the fields optional)

The enhancement should maintain backward compatibility and gracefully handle any boost periods that might not have associated creator information.

export type APIPath = keyof typeof API
export type APISchema<N extends APIPath> = (typeof API)[N]

export type APIParams<N extends APIPath> = z.input<APISchema<N>['props']>
export type ValidatedAPIParams<N extends APIPath> = z.output<
  APISchema<N>['props']
>

export type APIResponse<N extends APIPath> = APISchema<N> extends {
  returns: Record<string, any>
}
  ? APISchema<N>['returns']
  : void

export type APIResponseOptionalContinue<N extends APIPath> =
  | { continue: () => Promise<void>; result: APIResponse<N> }
  | APIResponse<N>

export type APIPath = keyof typeof API
export type APISchema<N extends APIPath> = (typeof API)[N]

export type APIParams<N extends APIPath> = z.input<APISchema<N>['props']>
export type ValidatedAPIParams<N extends APIPath> = z.output<
  APISchema<N>['props']
>

export type APIResponse<N extends APIPath> = APISchema<N> extends {
  returns: Record<string, any>
}
  ? APISchema<N>['returns']
  : void

export type APIResponseOptionalContinue<N extends APIPath> =
  | { continue: () => Promise<void>; result: APIResponse<N> }
  | APIResponse<N>

The post creation functionality needs to be updated with the following changes:

1. **API Schema Update**: Modify the `create-post` API endpoint validation to increase the maximum allowed title length from 120 characters to 160 characters.

2. **Enhanced Error Handling**: Improve the error handling in the post creation form to provide more specific validation error messages:
   - Import and use an `APIError` class/type from the API library
   - When an API error occurs during post creation, check if it's an `APIError` instance
   - If the error message contains 'validating request', extract field-specific validation details from the error
   - Display field-specific errors in the format "{field}: {error}" using the first validation error from the details
   - Fall back to showing the general error message if it's an `APIError` but not a validation error
   - Fall back to a generic error message for non-API errors
   - Log non-API errors to the console for debugging

The error handling should be able to parse validation errors that come in a structured format with field names and specific error messages, providing users with clear feedback about what needs to be corrected in their post submission.

export type APIPath = keyof typeof API
export type APISchema<N extends APIPath> = (typeof API)[N]

export type APIParams<N extends APIPath> = z.input<APISchema<N>['props']>
export type ValidatedAPIParams<N extends APIPath> = z.output<
  APISchema<N>['props']
>

export type APIResponse<N extends APIPath> = APISchema<N> extends {
  returns: Record<string, any>
}
  ? APISchema<N>['returns']
  : void

export type APIResponseOptionalContinue<N extends APIPath> =
  | { continue: () => Promise<void>; result: APIResponse<N> }
  | APIResponse<N>

The user last active time functionality needs to be modified to work with day-level granularity instead of precise timestamps:

**Backend Changes:**
- Modify the database query in the get-user-last-active-time API endpoint to truncate all timestamp fields (`last_card_view_ts`, `last_page_view_ts`, `last_promoted_view_ts`) to day-level precision before processing
- The truncation should be applied consistently in both the SELECT clause that calculates the maximum timestamp and the ORDER BY clause used for sorting
- The day truncation should occur before converting timestamps to milliseconds

**Frontend Changes:**
- Replace the existing relative timestamp component display for "Last active" with a custom formatting function
- Create a formatting function that converts timestamps to human-readable relative time strings with the following format rules:
  - 0 days difference: "today"
  - 1 day difference: "yesterday" 
  - 2-7 days: "X days ago"
  - 1-4 weeks: "X weeks ago" (with singular "1 week ago")
  - 1-12 months: "X months ago" (with singular "1 month ago")
  - Within a year but over 12 months: "in the last year"
  - Over a year: "over a year"
  - Zero timestamp: "Never"
- Apply this formatting function to display the last active time in the user hovercard instead of using the previous relative timestamp component

The changes should maintain the same data flow and API structure while changing how timestamps are processed and displayed.

Create a new API endpoint called `get-user-last-active-time` that retrieves a user's most recent activity timestamp from contract view tracking data.

**API Endpoint Requirements:**
- Endpoint path: `get-user-last-active-time`
- HTTP method: GET
- Authentication: Not required
- Visibility: Undocumented
- Cache strategy: Default cache strategy
- Input parameters: 
  - `userId` (string, required)
- Response format:
  - `{ lastActiveTime: number | null }`
  - Should return the timestamp in milliseconds, or null if no activity found

**Database Query Logic:**
- Query the `user_contract_views` table for the specified user ID
- Find the maximum (most recent) timestamp among these three fields:
  - `last_card_view_ts`
  - `last_page_view_ts` 
  - `last_promoted_view_ts`
- Convert timestamps to milliseconds using a `ts_to_millis` function
- Handle null values by treating them as 0 when comparing
- Only consider rows where at least one of the three timestamp fields is not null
- Return the highest timestamp value, or null if no valid timestamps exist

**Integration Requirements:**
- Add the endpoint to the API routes configuration
- Add the endpoint definition to the API schema with appropriate Zod validation
- The endpoint should be accessible via the standard API routing system

**Frontend Integration:**
- Update the user hovercard component to call this new API endpoint
- Combine the API response with the user's existing `lastBetTime` field to show the most recent activity
- Display "Last active:" followed by a relative timestamp for all users
- Show "Never" if no activity timestamp is available
- Remove any moderator-only restrictions on displaying this information

// with user willingness to put up with stale data
export const DEFAULT_CACHE_STRATEGY =
  'public, max-age=5, stale-while-revalidate=10'
// Light cache to prevent accidental rapid-fire requests from hitting the server fresh every time
export const LIGHT_CACHE_STRATEGY =
  'public, max-age=1, stale-while-revalidate=0'
const MAX_EXPIRES_AT = 1_000 * YEAR_MS

type APIGenericSchema = {
  // GET is for retrieval, POST is to mutate something, PUT is idempotent mutation (can be repeated safely)
  method: 'GET' | 'POST' | 'PUT'
  //private APIs can only be called from manifold. undocumented endpoints can change or be deleted at any time!
  visibility: 'public' | 'undocumented' | 'private'
  // whether the endpoint requires authentication
  authed: boolean
  // zod schema for the request body (or for params for GET requests)
  props: z.ZodType
  // note this has to be JSON serializable
  returns?: Record<string, any>
  // Cache-Control header. like, 'max-age=60'
  cache?: string
  // whether the endpoint should prefer authentication even if not required
  preferAuth?: boolean
}

export type APIPath = keyof typeof API
export type APISchema<N extends APIPath> = (typeof API)[N]

export type APIParams<N extends APIPath> = z.input<APISchema<N>['props']>
export type ValidatedAPIParams<N extends APIPath> = z.output<
  APISchema<N>['props']
>

export type APIResponse<N extends APIPath> = APISchema<N> extends {
  returns: Record<string, any>
}
  ? APISchema<N>['returns']
  : void

export type APIResponseOptionalContinue<N extends APIPath> =
  | { continue: () => Promise<void>; result: APIResponse<N> }
  | APIResponse<N>

export type APIPath = keyof typeof API
export type APISchema<N extends APIPath> = (typeof API)[N]

export type APIParams<N extends APIPath> = z.input<APISchema<N>['props']>
export type ValidatedAPIParams<N extends APIPath> = z.output<
  APISchema<N>['props']
>

export type APIResponse<N extends APIPath> = APISchema<N> extends {
  returns: Record<string, any>
}
  ? APISchema<N>['returns']
  : void

export type APIResponseOptionalContinue<N extends APIPath> =
  | { continue: () => Promise<void>; result: APIResponse<N> }
  | APIResponse<N>

evalCommits.spec:
Modify the metrics collection system to reduce metric cardinality by removing or categorizing high-cardinality labels:

**HTTP Request Metrics (app.ts)**
- In the request monitoring middleware, update the `metrics.inc` call for 'http/request_count' to only include `baseEndpoint` and `method` labels, removing the `endpoint` label
- In the request monitoring middleware, update the `metrics.push` call for 'http/request_latency' to only include `baseEndpoint` and `method` labels, removing the `endpoint` label

**PostgreSQL Query Metrics (supabase/init.ts)**
- In the pgPromise `transact` event handler, when monitoring context has a `baseEndpoint`, update the `metrics.push` call for 'pg/transaction_duration' to only include `baseEndpoint` and `successStr` labels, removing the `endpoint` and `query` labels
- In the pgPromise `transact` event handler, when monitoring context has a `job`, update the `metrics.push` call for 'pg/transaction_duration' to only include `job` and `successStr` labels, removing the `query` label
- In the pgPromise `transact` event handler, when there is no specific monitoring context, update the `metrics.push` call for 'pg/transaction_duration' to only include `successStr` label, removing the `query` label
- In the pgPromise `query` event handler, when monitoring context has a `baseEndpoint`, update the `metrics.inc` call for 'pg/query_count' to use `baseEndpoint` label instead of `endpoint`
- In the pgPromise `query` event handler, when monitoring context has a `job`, keep the existing `job` label
- In the pgPromise `query` event handler, when there is no specific monitoring context, keep the existing parameterless call

**WebSocket Broadcast Metrics (websockets/server.ts)**
- Add a new function `getTopicCategory` that categorizes websocket topics into predefined categories based on topic prefixes:
  - Topics starting with 'answer/' should return 'answer'
  - Topics starting with 'contract/' should return 'contract'  
  - Topics starting with 'user/' should return 'user'
  - Topics starting with 'private-user/' should return 'private-user'
  - Topics equal to 'global' or starting with 'global/' should return 'global'
  - Topics starting with 'post/' should return 'post'
  - All other topics should return 'other'
- In the `broadcastMulti` function, update the `metrics.inc` call for 'ws/broadcasts_sent' to use a `category` label with the categorized topic value instead of the raw `topic` label

The system needs to implement the following changes to handle concurrent bet placement during user metrics calculation:

1. **Remove Deprecation Warning Flag**: Remove the `FIXED_DEPRECATION_WARNING` boolean constant and its associated conditional check. The condition `if (USING_BETS && FIXED_DEPRECATION_WARNING)` should be simplified to `if (USING_BETS)`.

2. **Implement Batched User Processing**: Modify the user metrics update function to process users in batches of 100 instead of processing all users at once. The function should:

   - Excludes metric updates for users with concurrent bets from the current batch

   - Ensures each user is eventually processed when no concurrent bet activity occurs

5. **Update Contract Loading**: Replace the custom contract loading function with a call to `getContractsDirect()`, passing the contract IDs and database client as parameters.

The updated function should maintain the same external interface and overall behavior while resolving the race condition where users could place bets during metrics calculation, leading to inconsistent metric states.

# Comment Deletion Feature Implementation

## Overview
Implement a comment deletion feature that allows administrators and moderators to completely remove comments from display, as an alternative to the existing "hide" functionality which shows a "comment hidden" placeholder.

## API Changes

### Update hide-comment API Schema
- Modify the 'hide-comment' API endpoint to accept an optional `action` parameter
- `action` should be an enum with values 'hide' or 'delete', defaulting to 'hide'
- The API should maintain backward compatibility when no action is specified

### Update hide-comment API Logic
- Implement different permission checks based on action:
  - For 'delete' action: Only admins and moderators can delete comments
  - For 'hide' action: Contract creators, admins, and moderators can hide comments
- Add protection to prevent deletion of comments from administrators or moderators
- Update appropriate database fields based on action type:
  - Delete action: Update `deleted`, `deletedTime`, and `deleterId` fields
  - Hide action: Update `hidden`, `hiddenTime`, and `hiderId` fields (existing behavior)
- Track different analytics events: 'delete_comment' for delete action, 'hide_comment' for hide action

## Data Model Changes

### Comment Type Updates
- Add three new optional fields to the Comment type:
  - `deleted?: boolean` - indicates if the comment has been deleted
  - `deletedTime?: number` - timestamp when comment was deleted
  - `deleterId?: string` - ID of user who deleted the comment

## Database Query Updates

### Filter Deleted Comments
- Update all comment fetching functions to exclude deleted comments from results
- Add filter conditions like `.not('data->>deleted', 'eq', 'true')` to database queries
- Apply this filter to functions including:
  - getCommentsDirect
  - getPostAndContractComments
  - getRecentTopLevelCommentsAndReplies
  - getPinnedComments

  - getCommentRows
  - getNewCommentRows

## Frontend Changes

### Comment Rendering
- Modify comment components (FeedComment and ParentFeedComment) to return `null` when `comment.deleted` is true
- This should result in deleted comments being completely hidden from view with no placeholder or indication

### UI Controls
- Add a delete option to the comment dropdown menu
- Display the delete option only for moderators and administrators
- Use a trash icon with red styling to distinguish from hide option
- Implement optimistic updates that immediately hide the comment, with rollback on API failure
- Show appropriate success/error messages for delete operations

### API Integration
- Call the hide-comment API with `action='delete'` parameter for delete operations
- Handle API responses and errors appropriately
- Maintain existing hide functionality unchanged

## Behavioral Requirements

### Complete Removal vs Hide
- Deleted comments should be completely filtered out at the database level and not render at all
- Hidden comments should continue to show a "comment hidden" placeholder (existing behavior)
- Deleted comments should not appear in any comment lists or threads

### Permission Matrix
- Contract creators: Can hide comments, cannot delete comments
- Administrators: Can both hide and delete comments (except admin/mod comments)
- Moderators: Can both hide and delete comments (except admin/mod comments)
- Regular users: Cannot hide or delete other users' comments

### Data Preservation
- Deleted comments should remain in the database for audit purposes
- Include tracking of who deleted the comment and when
- Maintain audit trail through analytics events

### Error Handling
- Prevent deletion of comments by administrators or moderators
- Show appropriate error messages for permission failures
- Implement proper rollback for failed optimistic updates

import { convertContractComment } from 'common/supabase/comments'
import { SupabaseDirectClient } from 'shared/supabase/init'
import { APIError } from 'common/api/utils'
import { millisToTs } from 'common/supabase/utils'
import { ContractComment, PostComment } from 'common/comment'

export async function getCommentSafe(
  pg: SupabaseDirectClient,
  commentId: string
) {
  return pg.oneOrNone(
    `select data from contract_comments where comment_id = $1`,
    [commentId],
    (r) => (r ? convertContractComment(r.data) : null)
  )
}

export async function getComment(pg: SupabaseDirectClient, commentId: string) {
  const comment = await pg.oneOrNone(
    `select data from contract_comments where comment_id = $1`,
    [commentId],
    (r) => (r ? convertContractComment(r.data) : null)
  )
  if (!comment) {
    throw new APIError(404, 'Comment not found')
  }
  return comment
}

export async function getCommentsDirect(
  pg: SupabaseDirectClient,
  filters: {
    userId?: string
    contractId?: string
    limit?: number
    page?: number
    replyToCommentId?: string
    commentId?: string
    afterTime?: number
    order?: 'likes' | 'newest' | 'oldest'
  }
) {
  const {
    userId,
    contractId,
    limit = 5000,
    page = 0,
    replyToCommentId,
    commentId,
    afterTime,
    order = 'newest',
  } = filters

  const params: any[] = [
    limit,
    page * limit,
    contractId,
    userId,
    replyToCommentId,
    commentId,
    afterTime ? millisToTs(afterTime) : null,
  ]
  const orderBy =
    order === 'likes'
      ? 'cc.likes desc'
      : !order || order === 'newest'
      ? 'cc.created_time desc'
      : 'cc.created_time asc'

  return await pg.map(
    `
        select cc.data, cc.likes from contract_comments cc
          join contracts c on cc.contract_id = c.id
        where c.visibility = 'public'
          and ($3 is null or contract_id = $3)
          and ($4 is null or user_id = $4)
          and ($5 is null or cc.data->>'replyToCommentId' = $5) 
          and ($6 is null or cc.comment_id = $6)          
          and ($7 is null or cc.created_time > $7)        
        order by ${orderBy}
        limit $1
        offset $2
    `,
    params,
    convertContractComment
  )
}

export async function getPostAndContractComments(
  pg: SupabaseDirectClient,
  filters: {
    userId: string
    limit?: number
    page?: number
    afterTime?: number
  }
): Promise<(ContractComment | PostComment)[]> {
  const { userId, limit = 5000, page = 0, afterTime } = filters

  const params: any[] = [
    limit,
    page * limit,
    userId,
    afterTime ? millisToTs(afterTime) : null,
  ]

  const query = `
      SELECT * FROM (
        -- Contract Comments
        SELECT
            cc.data,
            cc.created_time,
            cc.comment_id,
            c.slug,
            c.question as title
        FROM contract_comments cc
        JOIN contracts c ON cc.contract_id = c.id
        WHERE
            c.visibility = 'public'
            AND cc.user_id = $3                   -- userId (must be present here)
            AND ($4 IS NULL OR cc.created_time > $4) -- afterTime
            
        UNION ALL

        -- Old Post Comments
        SELECT
            opc.data,
            opc.created_time,
            opc.comment_id,
            op.data->>'slug' as slug,
            op.data->>'title' as title
        FROM old_post_comments opc
        join old_posts op on opc.post_id = op.id
        WHERE
            opc.user_id = $3
            AND ($4 IS NULL OR opc.created_time > $4)
            and op.visibility = 'public'
      ) AS combined_comments
      ORDER BY created_time DESC
      LIMIT $1 -- limit
      OFFSET $2 -- offset
    `

  return await pg.map(query, params, (r) => {
    const comment = r.data as ContractComment | PostComment
    if (comment.commentType === 'post') {
      comment.postSlug = r.slug
      comment.postTitle = r.title
    }
    return comment
  })
}

# Comment Deletion Feature Implementation Summary

## Overview
Added a new "delete" option to the comments dropdown menu that allows admins/mods to completely hide comments from rendering, rather than just showing "comment hidden" like the existing hide functionality.

## Key Features
- **Admin/Mod Only**: Delete functionality is restricted to admins and moderators only (more restrictive than hide)
- **Complete Removal**: Deleted comments are completely filtered out and don't render at all
- **Preservation of Hide**: Existing hide functionality remains unchanged for less severe moderation
- **Protection**: Prevents deletion of admin/mod comments by other users

## Technical Implementation

### 1. Data Model Changes
**File**: `common/src/comment.ts`
- Added `deleted?: boolean` field to Comment type
- Added `deletedTime?: number` field for tracking deletion timestamp  
- Added `deleterId?: string` field for tracking who deleted the comment

### 2. API Schema Updates
**File**: `common/src/api/schema.ts`
- Modified `hide-comment` API to accept optional `action` parameter
- Action values: `'hide'` (default) or `'delete'`

### 3. Backend API Logic
**File**: `backend/api/src/hide-comment.ts`
- **Delete Action**: Only admins/mods can delete (not contract creators)
- **Hide Action**: Contract creators, admins, and mods can hide
- Added protection against deleting admin/mod comments
- Proper tracking events for both actions
- Updates appropriate database fields based on action type

### 4. Frontend Components

#### Comment Rendering
**Files**: `web/components/comments/comment.tsx`
- `FeedComment` and `ParentFeedComment` return `null` for deleted comments
- `HideableContent` component skips rendering deleted comments entirely

#### UI Controls
**File**: `web/components/comments/comment-header.tsx`
- Added delete option to dropdown menu (mods only)
- Uses TrashIcon with red color styling
- Calls hide-comment API with `action='delete'`
- Includes optimistic updates and error handling

### 5. Database Query Updates
**Files**: Multiple comment fetching functions updated
- `backend/shared/src/supabase/contract-comments.ts`
- `common/src/supabase/comments.ts`
- `web/lib/supabase/comments.ts`

**Query Modifications**: All comment queries now filter out deleted comments using conditions like:
```sql
.not('data->>deleted', 'eq', 'true')
-- or
(cc.data->>'deleted' is null or cc.data->>'deleted' = 'false')
```

**Affected Functions**:
- `getCommentsDirect`
- `getPostAndContractComments` 
- `getRecentTopLevelCommentsAndReplies`
- `getPinnedComments`
- `getCommentThread`
- `getAllCommentRows`
- `getCommentRows`
- `getNewCommentRows`
- `getRecentCommentsOnContracts`

## Permission Matrix

| Action | Contract Creator | Admin | Mod |
|--------|-----------------|-------|-----|
| Hide Comment | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Delete Comment | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Delete Admin/Mod Comment | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ |

## User Experience
- **Seamless Removal**: Deleted comments completely disappear from view
- **Optimistic Updates**: UI responds immediately with rollback on API failure
- **Clear Distinction**: Different visual treatment (TrashIcon) for delete vs hide actions
- **No Placeholder**: Unlike hidden comments, deleted comments show no trace

## Data Integrity
- Maintains audit trail with `deletedTime` and `deleterId` fields
- Comments remain in database for potential recovery/audit purposes
- Proper tracking events ensure moderation actions are logged
- Database-level filtering prevents accidental exposure of deleted content

## Benefits
1. **Stronger Moderation**: More severe action than hiding for problematic content
2. **Clean User Experience**: Complete removal vs. "comment hidden" placeholder
3. **Granular Control**: Different permission levels for hide vs delete
4. **Audit Trail**: Full tracking of deletion actions for accountability
5. **Performance**: Database-level filtering reduces unnecessary data processing

export type APIPath = keyof typeof API
export type APISchema<N extends APIPath> = (typeof API)[N]

export type APIParams<N extends APIPath> = z.input<APISchema<N>['props']>
export type ValidatedAPIParams<N extends APIPath> = z.output<
  APISchema<N>['props']
>

export type APIResponse<N extends APIPath> = APISchema<N> extends {
  returns: Record<string, any>
}
  ? APISchema<N>['returns']
  : void

export type APIResponseOptionalContinue<N extends APIPath> =
  | { continue: () => Promise<void>; result: APIResponse<N> }
  | APIResponse<N>

export type APIPath = keyof typeof API
export type APISchema<N extends APIPath> = (typeof API)[N]

export type APIParams<N extends APIPath> = z.input<APISchema<N>['props']>
export type ValidatedAPIParams<N extends APIPath> = z.output<
  APISchema<N>['props']
>

export type APIResponse<N extends APIPath> = APISchema<N> extends {
  returns: Record<string, any>
}
  ? APISchema<N>['returns']
  : void

export type APIResponseOptionalContinue<N extends APIPath> =
  | { continue: () => Promise<void>; result: APIResponse<N> }
  | APIResponse<N>

Add a minimum bet amount filter capability to the bets API and user interface.

## API Changes

1. **Bets API endpoint** (`/bets`) should accept a new optional parameter:
   - `minAmount`: A positive number representing the minimum bet amount threshold
   - When provided, only return bets where the absolute value of the bet amount is greater than or equal to this threshold

2. **Backend filtering logic** should:
   - Extract the `minAmount` parameter from the API request
   - Pass it to the bet filtering function
   - Apply a SQL WHERE condition that filters bets based on: `abs((contract_bets.data->>'amount')::numeric) >= minAmount`
   - Only apply this filter when `minAmount` is defined

## User Interface Changes

3. **Bet tab in contract pages** should include:
   - A dropdown filter with minimum amount options: "Any amount", "M$100+", "M$1,000+", "M$10,000+"
   - The filter should be positioned in the top-right area of the bets tab
   - Filter selection should persist across page visits for each contract
   - When filter changes, clear existing loaded bets and reload with new filter

4. **Bet loading behavior** should:
   - Apply client-side filtering to initially loaded bets based on selected minimum amount
   - Apply server-side filtering when loading additional older bets via API calls
   - Use infinite scroll instead of pagination for loading more bets
   - Track user interactions with the amount filter for analytics

5. **Filter state management** should:
   - Remember the selected filter option per contract using persistent storage
   - Reset loaded bets when filter changes to ensure consistency
   - Pass the selected minimum amount to API calls when loading more bets

The implementation should maintain existing bet display functionality while adding the ability to filter by bet amount threshold both on the client and server sides.

export type APIPath = keyof typeof API
export type APISchema<N extends APIPath> = (typeof API)[N]

export type APIParams<N extends APIPath> = z.input<APISchema<N>['props']>
export type ValidatedAPIParams<N extends APIPath> = z.output<
  APISchema<N>['props']
>

export type APIResponse<N extends APIPath> = APISchema<N> extends {
  returns: Record<string, any>
}
  ? APISchema<N>['returns']
  : void

export type APIResponseOptionalContinue<N extends APIPath> =
  | { continue: () => Promise<void>; result: APIResponse<N> }
  | APIResponse<N>

export type APIPath = keyof typeof API
export type APISchema<N extends APIPath> = (typeof API)[N]

export type APIParams<N extends APIPath> = z.input<APISchema<N>['props']>
export type ValidatedAPIParams<N extends APIPath> = z.output<
  APISchema<N>['props']
>

export type APIResponse<N extends APIPath> = APISchema<N> extends {
  returns: Record<string, any>
}
  ? APISchema<N>['returns']
  : void

export type APIResponseOptionalContinue<N extends APIPath> =
  | { continue: () => Promise<void>; result: APIResponse<N> }
  | APIResponse<N>

## Post Boosting System

Extend the existing contract boosting functionality to support boosting posts. Posts should be able to be boosted in the same way as contracts to increase their visibility on the homepage.

### Core Functionality

**Boost Purchasing:**
- Users should be able to purchase boosts for posts using mana (internal currency), cash (via Stripe), or free admin boosts
- Boosts should last for 24 hours from the specified start time
- Users should be able to schedule boosts to start at a future date
- Only admins and moderators can apply free boosts
- Posts must be public (not unlisted) to be eligible for boosting

**API Endpoint:**
- Modify the existing boost purchase endpoint to accept either a `contractId` OR a `postId` parameter (mutually exclusive)
- Validate that exactly one of these parameters is provided
- Support the same payment methods: 'mana', 'cash', 'admin-free'
- Return a checkout URL for cash payments via Stripe
- Handle immediate boost activation if the start time is now or in the past

**Database Schema:**
- Update the `contract_boosts` table to support both contracts and posts:
  - Make `contract_id` column optional (nullable)
  - Add optional `post_id` column referencing posts
  - Add constraint ensuring exactly one of `contract_id` or `post_id` is provided
  - Add `created_time` and `funded` columns for payment tracking
- Add `boosted` boolean column to posts table, defaulting to false

**Post Data Model:**
- Posts should include a `boosted` boolean field indicating current boost status
- When creating new posts, initialize `boosted` as false

**Importance Scoring:**
- Include post boosts in the importance scoring algorithm
- Boosted posts should receive higher importance scores and appear more prominently on the homepage
- Query active post boosts when calculating post importance scores

**Payment Processing:**
- Stripe webhooks should handle both contract and post boost payments
- Update transaction records to support post boosts (include `postId` in transaction data)
- Support the same mana cost and $100 cash price as contract boosts

**User Interface:**
- Add boost button to post pages that shows "Boost" or "Boosted" based on current status
- Post boost purchase modal should mirror the contract boost modal functionality
- Show boost status indicator in post listings (similar to contract boost indicators)
- Support the same date picker and payment options as contract boosting

**Content Validation:**
- Only allow boosting of public posts (not unlisted posts)
- Ensure posts exist and are accessible before allowing boost purchase
- Validate user permissions (authentication required)

### Integration Points

**Existing Systems:**
- Leverage the existing boost infrastructure used for contracts
- Reuse boost analytics, scheduling, and payment processing logic
- Maintain consistency with contract boost pricing and duration
- Use the same Stripe integration and webhook handling

**Homepage Display:**
- Boosted posts should appear more prominently in post feeds
- Boost status should be visually indicated in post listings
- Include boosted posts in importance-based sorting algorithms

# API Endpoints

This directory contains the implementation of various API endpoints for the Manifold platform.

## Key Concepts

- Each endpoint is typically implemented in its own file.
- The `routes.ts` file serves as the main router, connecting endpoint handlers to their respective routes.
- We use Supabase for database operations.
- Authentication is handled using the `APIHandler` type, which automatically manages user authentication based on the schema definition.

## Mana/Sweepstakes Market Relationships

- Mana markets can have sweepstakes counterpart markets (siblingContractId)
- The mana market is the source of truth - changes to mana markets should propagate to their sweepstakes counterparts
- Changes that need to propagate include:
  - Adding new answers to multiple choice markets
  - Market metadata updates
  - Market resolution

## Adding a New API Endpoint

To add a new API endpoint, follow these steps:

1. Create a new file for the endpoint in the `backend/api/src` directory. Each endpoint should be in a new file.
2. Implement the endpoint logic in the new file.
3. Add the endpoint schema to `common/src/api/schema.ts`, including props, return type, and other information. Note that we only use POST and GET methods.
4. Update `backend/api/src/routes.ts`:
   - Import the handler function from the new file.
   - Add the handler to the `handlers` object.

Example:

```typescript
// 1. Create a new file: backend/api/src/my-new-endpoint.ts
import { APIHandler } from 'api/helpers/endpoint'

export const myNewEndpoint: APIHandler<'my-new-endpoint'> = async (props, auth, req) => {
  // Implement endpoint logic here
}

// 2. Add to common/src/api/schema.ts
'my-new-endpoint': {
  method: 'POST',
  visibility: 'public',
  authed: true,
  props: z.object({
    // Define props here using Zod schema
  }),
  returns: z.object({
    // Define return type here using Zod schema
  }),
},

// 3. Update backend/api/src/routes.ts
import { myNewEndpoint } from './my-new-endpoint'

const handlers: { [k in APIPath]: APIHandler<k> } = {
  // ... existing handlers
  'my-new-endpoint': myNewEndpoint,
}
```

## Authentication

Authentication is managed automatically by the `APIHandler` type. The `authed` property in the schema determines the authentication behavior:

- `false`: The endpoint can be called without authentication.
- `true`: The endpoint requires authentication. The `auth` object will be provided to the handler function.

Example of an authenticated endpoint:

```typescript
export const myAuthenticatedEndpoint: APIHandler<
  'my-authenticated-endpoint'
> = async (props, auth, req) => {
  const { uid } = auth // auth object is automatically provided for authenticated endpoints
  // Implement endpoint logic here
}
```

## Best Practices

- Use the `createSupabaseDirectClient` function from `shared/supabase/init` for database operations.
- For environment-specific IDs and constants, check common/antes.ts first as it contains important platform-wide constants like HOUSE_LIQUIDITY_PROVIDER_ID.


## Sports Markets

- Each sports event can have at most one MANA market and one CASH market
- If creation of the MANA market fails (e.g., due to duplicate sportsEventId), do not attempt to create the CASH market
- The MANA market is considered the "source of truth" - the CASH market should only exist if there is a corresponding MANA market
- Prefer lightweight check endpoints over complex validation in create/update endpoints when the check might be useful in other contexts

  This uses the pg promise library, where you pass raw sql strings like so:

```ts
import { createSupabaseClient } from 'shared/supabase/init'

const pg = createSupabaseDirectConnection()
const contractIds = await pg.manyOrNone(
  `select id from contracts`,
  [],
  (r) => r.id as string
)
```

- Keep endpoint logic modular and reusable when possible.
- Use TypeScript types consistently to ensure type safety across the API.
- Use Zod schemas in `common/src/api/schema.ts` to define prop and return types for strong type checking.
- Use the `APIError` class from `api/helpers/endpoint` to throw standardized API errors.
- Use lowercase SQL keywords in queries. Don't capitalize SQL keywords.
- Avoid editing the SQL via `${}`, and instead when using pgpromise, use the argument following the query to pass parameters to the query.

### Schema Definition

We use Zod for defining our API schemas. This provides runtime type checking and automatic documentation generation.

#### Setting Defaults

When defining schemas, prefer setting defaults in the Zod schema rather than in the handler function. This ensures that the default values are documented and type-checked.

Example:

```typescript
props: z.object({
  limit: z.number().default(50),
  offset: z.number().default(0),
  // other properties...
}).strict(),
```

### Data schema

Tables like contract_comments, contract_bets, contract_follows, etc, use two primary ids: contract_id, and an id specific to the table: comment_id, bet_id, or follow_id. Thus they have no primary 'id' column.

Thus to get a comment you would do:

```sql
select * from contract_comments where comment_id = $1
```

### Query Construction

For constructing SQL queries, we use custom SQL builder helper functions. These functions provide a more type-safe and maintainable way to build complex queries.

#### SQL Builder Functions

Use the sqlBuilder from `shared/supabase/sql-builder.ts` for constructing SQL queries with re-useable components. It has several helper functions for building SQL queries, including:

- `select`: Specifies the columns to select
- `from`: Specifies the table to query
- `where`: Adds WHERE clauses
- `orderBy`: Specifies the order of results
- `limit`: Limits the number of results
- `renderSql`: Combines all parts into a final SQL string

Example usage:

```typescript
const query = renderSql(
  select('*'),
  from('txns'),
  where('token = ${token}', { token }),
  orderBy('created_time desc'),
  limit(limitValue)
)
```

Using these functions instead of string concatenation helps prevent SQL injection and makes queries easier to read and maintain.

export type APIPath = keyof typeof API
export type APISchema<N extends APIPath> = (typeof API)[N]

export type APIParams<N extends APIPath> = z.input<APISchema<N>['props']>
export type ValidatedAPIParams<N extends APIPath> = z.output<
  APISchema<N>['props']
>

export type APIResponse<N extends APIPath> = APISchema<N> extends {
  returns: Record<string, any>
}
  ? APISchema<N>['returns']
  : void

export type APIResponseOptionalContinue<N extends APIPath> =
  | { continue: () => Promise<void>; result: APIResponse<N> }
  | APIResponse<N>

type APIGenericSchema = {

  //private APIs can only be called from manifold. undocumented endpoints can change or be deleted at any time!
  visibility: 'public' | 'undocumented' | 'private'

  authed: boolean

  props: z.ZodType

  returns?: Record<string, any>
  // Cache-Control header. like, 'max-age=60'
  cache?: string

  preferAuth?: boolean

export type APIPath = keyof typeof API
export type APISchema<N extends APIPath> = (typeof API)[N]

export type APIParams<N extends APIPath> = z.input<APISchema<N>['props']>
export type ValidatedAPIParams<N extends APIPath> = z.output<
  APISchema<N>['props']
>

export type APIResponse<N extends APIPath> = APISchema<N> extends {
  returns: Record<string, any>
}
  ? APISchema<N>['returns']
  : void

export type APIResponseOptionalContinue<N extends APIPath> =
  | { continue: () => Promise<void>; result: APIResponse<N> }
  | APIResponse<N>

import { JSONContent } from '@tiptap/core'

import { ENV_CONFIG } from './envs/constants'
import { referralQuery } from './util/share'

export type TopLevelPost = {
  id: string
  type?: string
  title: string
  /** @deprecated */
  subtitle?: string
  content: JSONContent
  creatorId: string // User id
  createdTime: number
  slug: string

  // denormalized user fields
  creatorName: string
  creatorUsername: string
  creatorAvatarUrl?: string

  likedByUserIds?: string[]
  likedByUserCount?: number

  /** @deprecated */
  commentCount?: number
  /** @deprecated */
  isGroupAboutPost?: boolean
  groupId?: string
  featuredLabel?: string
  visibility: Visibility
  unlistedById?: string
  isAnnouncement?: boolean
  isChangeLog?: boolean
  /** @deprecated - not deprecated, only updated in native column though*/
  importanceScore: number
  /** @deprecated - not deprecated, only available via the get-posts endpoint*/
  uniqueUsers?: number
}

export const convertPost = (sqlPost: Row<'old_posts'>) =>
  convertSQLtoTS<'old_posts', TopLevelPost>(sqlPost, {
    created_time: false, // grab from data
  })

export const getPostShareUrl = (
  post: TopLevelPost,
  username: string | undefined
) =>
  `https://${ENV_CONFIG.domain}/post/${post.slug}${
    username ? referralQuery(username) : ''
  }`
export const getPostCommentShareUrl = (post: TopLevelPost, commentId: string) =>
  `https://${ENV_CONFIG.domain}/post/${post.slug}#${commentId}`

The purchase-contract-boost API endpoint needs to be enhanced to support a new "admin-free" payment method that allows administrators and moderators to boost contracts without any payment.

**API Schema Changes:**
- The `purchase-contract-boost` endpoint's `method` parameter should accept a third option: `'admin-free'` in addition to the existing `'mana'` and `'cash'` options

**Backend Authorization and Logic:**
- When the method is `'admin-free'`, the system should verify that the requesting user has admin or moderator privileges
- If a non-admin/non-mod user attempts to use the `'admin-free'` method, return a 403 error with message "Only admins and mods can use free boosts"
- For admin-free boosts, the boost should be created and marked as funded without processing any mana transaction
- All other boost functionality (time validation, boost creation, analytics tracking, immediate boosting) should work identically to paid boosts

**Frontend UI Changes:**
- In the boost purchase modal, when the current user is an admin or moderator, display an additional button labeled "Free Admin Boost"
- This admin-only button should call the API with `method: 'admin-free'`
- The button should have the same loading states and error handling as the other payment methods
- The admin boost button should be styled differently (e.g., outline style) and include a rocket icon
- On successful admin boost, show a success message indicating it was boosted for free

**Permission Requirements:**
- The system should use existing admin/mod identification functions to determine user privileges
- Only users identified as admins or mods should see and be able to use the free boost option
- The authorization check should happen both on the frontend (for UI display) and backend (for security)

**Behavior Consistency:**
- Admin-free boosts should create the same boost record structure as paid boosts
- The boost duration, analytics tracking, and visibility effects should be identical regardless of payment method
- Error handling for timing conflicts, market eligibility, etc. should work the same way

export const DEFAULT_CACHE_STRATEGY =
  'public, max-age=5, stale-while-revalidate=10'
// Light cache to prevent accidental rapid-fire requests from hitting the server fresh every time
export const LIGHT_CACHE_STRATEGY =
  'public, max-age=1, stale-while-revalidate=0'
const MAX_EXPIRES_AT = 1_000 * YEAR_MS

type APIGenericSchema = {
  // GET is for retrieval, POST is to mutate something, PUT is idempotent mutation (can be repeated safely)
  method: 'GET' | 'POST' | 'PUT'
  //private APIs can only be called from manifold. undocumented endpoints can change or be deleted at any time!
  visibility: 'public' | 'undocumented' | 'private'
  // whether the endpoint requires authentication
  authed: boolean
  // zod schema for the request body (or for params for GET requests)
  props: z.ZodType
  // note this has to be JSON serializable
  returns?: Record<string, any>
  // Cache-Control header. like, 'max-age=60'
  cache?: string
  // whether the endpoint should prefer authentication even if not required
  preferAuth?: boolean
}

export type APIPath = keyof typeof API
export type APISchema<N extends APIPath> = (typeof API)[N]

export type APIParams<N extends APIPath> = z.input<APISchema<N>['props']>
export type ValidatedAPIParams<N extends APIPath> = z.output<
  APISchema<N>['props']
>

export type APIResponse<N extends APIPath> = APISchema<N> extends {
  returns: Record<string, any>
}
  ? APISchema<N>['returns']
  : void

export type APIResponseOptionalContinue<N extends APIPath> =
  | { continue: () => Promise<void>; result: APIResponse<N> }
  | APIResponse<N>

  returns?: Record<string, any>

export type APIPath = keyof typeof API

export type APIParams<N extends APIPath> = z.input<APISchema<N>['props']>
export type ValidatedAPIParams<N extends APIPath> = z.output<
  APISchema<N>['props']
>

export type APIResponse<N extends APIPath> = APISchema<N> extends {
  returns: Record<string, any>
}
  ? APISchema<N>['returns']
  : void

export type APIResponseOptionalContinue<N extends APIPath> =
  | { continue: () => Promise<void>; result: APIResponse<N> }
  | APIResponse<N>
